**The file isn't foreign to Entire, but it is foreign to *this* installer** — it's a stale hand-written extension that's committed to entiredb's git:

```
fa702c7ac  Georg Friedrich  Sat Apr 11 2026  entire: Add pi agent
```

`InstallHooks` decides ownership by substring-matching a header comment (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/hooks.go:82`):

```
Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent pi`
```

That header has been in the embedded template since the in-tree pi integration landed (61c0f6144). The entiredb file has no header at all — it starts straight at the import — so the check can't recognize it and correctly refuses.

The committed copy is also genuinely out of date, not just unmarked:

| | entiredb (64 lines) | current template (127 lines) |
|---|---|---|
| import | `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` | `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` |
| exec | `execFileSync` (blocking) | `execFile` |
| hooks | 5 | 6 — adds `input` |

The package rename alone means it probably doesn't load under current pi.

## Fix

Overwrite it, from the entiredb repo:

```
! cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/entiredb && entire agent add pi --force
```

`--force` skips the ownership check entirely (`agent_group.go:125` → `ForceHooks`). Since the file is **tracked** in entiredb, this will show up as a modification you'll want to commit — that's the desired outcome, it replaces the hand-rolled version with the generated one.

One thing worth deciding: whether entiredb should keep `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` checked in at all. It's a generated artifact that every `entire agent add pi` will rewrite, so it'll churn against whatever CLI version each person has installed. Gitignoring it and letting `entire agent add pi` generate it per-clone would avoid that — but that's entiredb's call, not something I'd change from here.

Agreed — committed is the right call, and that changes what the actual bug is here.

## Immediate unblock

`--force` once, from entiredb:

```
! cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/entiredb && entire agent add pi --force
```

That's a one-time cost. After it, the file carries the `Auto-generated by...` header, and `InstallHooks` (`pi/hooks.go:76-85`) will silently rewrite it on any future content change — marker present + content differs → falls through to the write. So nobody hits this error again on that repo.

## But the real problem your constraint exposes

Committing the file makes staleness the failure mode, and **nothing detects it for pi**.

`PiAgent.AreHooksInstalled` (`pi/hooks.go:113`) only checks that the marker substring is present. It never compares against what the current template would write. So a committed extension that's marked-but-years-old reads as perfectly healthy forever — and `fireHook` swallows every error by design (`catch {}` / best-effort), so a broken extension is silent. That's exactly your "forgetting it means losing sessions", except worse: nobody forgot anything, and there's no signal.

This is already what happened in entiredb. The committed file imports `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`, which pi renamed to `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. If that fails to resolve, no hooks fire, `entire status` still reports pi hooks installed.

Claude Code is the only agent that handles this — `CheckHookConfig` returns `HooksAbsent`/`HooksCurrent`/`HooksOutdated` (`claudecode/hooks.go:470`), surfaced in `status.go:202,806` and `doctor.go:444`. And the status JSON field is already plural and general:

```go
// status.go:739
HooksOutdated []string `json:"hooks_outdated,omitempty"`
```

It's just only ever populated with `"claude-code"`. Pi and OpenCode both use the marker-only check and never appear there.

## Suggested fix

Give pi a `CheckHookConfig` equivalent and append `"pi"` to that existing `HooksOutdated` slice. One wrinkle: comparing full content breaks for local-dev installs, since `renderExtension(localDev)` substitutes `go run …` vs `entire` — a dev would show permanent false drift against the committed production file. Cleaner to stamp a template version into the header line and compare that, since it's identical across both renders:

```
// Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent pi` (template v3)
```

Then `entire status` in a fresh entiredb clone with a stale committed extension says so, and points at `entire agent add pi --force`.

Want me to build that? It's contained — the pi check plus wiring into the two existing call sites in status/doctor. OpenCode has the identical gap and could ride along, though its `InstallHooks` has no foreign-file guard at all so it silently self-heals on overwrite.

Built and verified. `mise run check` passes clean (lint 0 issues, unit + integration + canary E2E green).

## What I built

A shared `HookFreshness` capability rather than a pi-specific check, since the hardcoded `claudecode` branches in status/doctor were the thing that made this a one-agent feature:

- **`agent/agent.go`** — `HookConfigState` (Absent/Current/Outdated) + `HookFreshness` interface, alongside `HookSupport`.
- **`agent/hook_command.go`** — `GeneratedHookFileState(path, marker, renders...)`, shared by every agent whose config is one generated file.
- **pi, opencode** — implement `CheckHookConfig`. claudecode's existing enum became a type alias of the shared one, so its call sites and tests were untouched.
- **status/doctor** — now iterate installed agents via `AsHookFreshness` instead of naming claude-code. `hooks_outdated` in `--json` needed no schema change; it was already `[]string`.

I dropped the version-stamp idea from my earlier proposal. Comparing exact content against both renders (`renderExtension(false)` and `renderExtension(true)`) is strictly better: it catches *any* template edit automatically, with no version constant anyone can forget to bump. `LocalDevHookScript` is a fixed const, so matching either render is exact and machine-independent — that's what keeps local-dev installs from reading as permanent false drift.

A foreign file reads as `HooksAbsent`, not `Outdated` — `InstallHooks` refuses to touch it, so warning about it would nag about a file the CLI won't fix.

## It caught real drift immediately

```
$ entire status   # in entiredb
  Agents · Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi
  ! Claude Code hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
  ! OpenCode hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
  ! Pi hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
```

You've since run `--force` on the pi file, so it's regenerated (currently modified-unstaged in entiredb). It's still flagged because your installed `entire` predates ed42608db — it wrote `const ENTIRE_CMD = "entire"` with double quotes, and the current template uses single quotes. That's exactly the class of silent breakage you were worried about, caught rather than swallowed.

## One correction and one caveat

I overstated the current entiredb state earlier: I said the stale file reports as healthy. It didn't — the pre-`--force` file lacked the marker entirely, so `AreHooksInstalled` returned false and pi wasn't listed at all. The false-healthy window is the one that opens *after* the marker is present, which is where the file sits now and what the drift check covers.

The caveat: drift is measured against the checking binary's template. With a committed extension and a team on mixed CLI versions, whoever runs the newest CLI sees the warning until someone re-runs `--force` and commits. That's the correct signal for your setup — the committed file should track the newest template — but it does mean a yellow line rather than silence during version skew.

## Why

`entire agent add pi` in a repo with a committed extension failed with:

```
failed to setup pi hooks: refusing to overwrite foreign file at
  .pi/extensions/entire/index.ts; remove it or pass --force
```

That refusal was correct — the file predated the `Auto-generated by ...` header, so the installer couldn't recognise it as Entire's. But chasing it surfaced a real gap behind it.

Repos commonly **commit** `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`, so every clone gets checkpointing without each person enabling it by hand — forgetting to enable means losing sessions. The committed copy then goes stale as the template evolves, and nothing notices:

- `AreHooksInstalled` only checks for the marker substring, so a stale-but-marked file reads as installed forever.
- The extension's own `fireHook` swallows every error by design, so broken hooks are silent.

Result: the repo reports healthy while its hooks no-op. Claude Code was the only agent with a drift check (`CheckHookConfig`), and `status`/`doctor` hardcoded it by name, so no other agent could ever report drift regardless of what it implemented.

## What changed

- **`agent.HookFreshness`** — optional capability answering "is what's installed still what we'd write today?", distinct from `AreHooksInstalled`'s "is Entire wired up here at all?".
- **`agent.GeneratedHookFileState`** — shared implementation for agents whose whole integration is one generated file.
- **pi + opencode** implement it; **claudecode**'s enum becomes an alias of the shared type (no behaviour change, existing call sites untouched).
- **`status` + `doctor`** iterate installed agents via `AsHookFreshness` instead of naming claude-code. `status --json`'s `hooks_outdated` was already a list of agent names, so no schema change.

### Design note

Drift is detected by comparing **exact content against every render `InstallHooks` could have written**, not a stamped template version. Any edit to an embedded template then makes installed copies read as outdated automatically, with no version constant anyone can forget to bump. Matching both the production and local-dev renders is what keeps a `--local-dev` install from reading as permanent drift (`LocalDevHookScript` is a fixed const, so this is exact and machine-independent).

A **foreign** file reads as `HooksAbsent`, not `HooksOutdated` — `InstallHooks` refuses to overwrite it, so warning would nag about a file the CLI won't fix.

`mise run check` passes (lint 0 issues; unit + integration + canary E2E green). Each of the four commits builds independently, so bisect stays clean.

It found genuine drift on first run against a real repo:

```

  ! Claude Code hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
  ! OpenCode hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
  ! Pi hooks out of date · run 'entire enable --force'
```

The pi entry was a committed extension written before ed42608db (`ENTIRE_CMD` double-quoted instead of single-quoted) — exactly the silent-breakage class this is meant to catch.

## Trade-off worth a reviewer's eye

Drift is measured against **the checking binary's** template. With a committed extension and a team on mixed CLI versions, whoever runs the newest CLI sees the warning until someone re-runs `--force` and commits. That's the intended signal for a committed generated file, but it does mean a yellow status line during version skew rather than silence.

- **`stringutil`** has `CollapseWhitespace`, `TruncateRunes`, `CapitalizeFirst`. `CollapseWhitespace` handles `\r\n` but collapses *all* whitespace runs to a single space and trims — far too lossy here. It would make two genuinely different templates compare equal if they differed only in indentation or blank lines, which would silently disable drift detection.
- The `\r` handling that does exist (~9 sites: `trail_checkout_worktree.go:183`, `githelper/run.go:49`, etc.) is all **per-line** `TrimRight(line, "\r")` *inside* a split loop over subprocess output — a different shape that doesn't apply to comparing two whole file contents.

So it's genuinely new. I kept it unexported in `agent` next to its only caller rather than exporting it from `stringutil`, since it has one use and its doc comment is specific to the committed-file/autocrlf case. Say the word if you'd rather it live in `stringutil` so the next person finds it instead of hand-rolling one.

git add -A && git commit -q --no-gpg-sign -F - <<'EOF'
fix(agent): normalize line endings before comparing generated hook files

Bugbot and Copilot both caught this, and it is real: these files are
generated with LF but are typically committed, so on Windows a checkout
under git's default core.autocrlf=true hands us CRLF and byte equality
never holds.

That produced permanent drift the user could not clear — InstallHooks
writes LF back, and the next checkout converts it to CRLF again — on
exactly the committed-file setup this check exists to serve. The unit
tests missed it because they write the file through InstallHooks, which
never goes through git's conversion.

Lone CR is deliberately left alone: no generator here emits it, and
rewriting it would mask content that is genuinely different.

Also drop a misleading claim from the OutdatedHookAgents doc comment. It
said an agent whose config exists in the repo but that nobody enabled
stays quiet; for generated-file agents the committed file *is* the
installation, so such a repo does get warned. That is intended — it is
relying on the committed file to work — but the comment said otherwise.

Rename the doctor drift tests, which still carried the Claude-Code-only
name after the check was generalized.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
